newsitem.title: USA: IBM unveils program to lower PC costs.
newsitem.headline: IBM unveils program to lower PC costs.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. on Monday unveiled a major programme aimed at lowering the cost of owning, maintaining and upgrading personal computers for its corporate customers.

Under the one-stop shopping programme, dubbed SystemCare, customers can lease PC hardware for a monthly fee that will cover financing, service, maintenance, support and upgrades, the computer giant said.
The programme is aimed at small to medium-size businesses.
"I believe you can save between 25 to 40 percent (of current technology management costs)," Sam Palmisano, general manager of the IBM PC Co. business unit, said in a telephone interview.
Palmisano, who was once the head of IBM's services business, said the exact savings will depend on what kind of computer systems are already installed at a customer's site.

IBM said SystemCare is a package of the latest in PC hardware and network management software, competitively priced with flexible financing options, and extensive services and support. The IBM Credit Corp. will work closely with the PC Co. and authorised IBM resellers.
A key feature of the programme is the SystemCare Technology Exchange, which allows customers to upgrade their IBM PC hardware after only two years.
The Gartner Group estimates the total cost of PC ownership at $13,187 annually over a three-year life cycle.

"You have heard a lot about cost of ownership and we are doing more than that," Palmisano said, adding that IBM is not only addressing the changing technology but maintenance, help desk service, local area network monitoring and management.
